title: Nanovial Kits for Large-Scale Cell-Cell Interaction Sequencing
text:
This project delivers accessible tools that link functional cell–cell behavior to gene expression at large scale
using standard lab equipment and off-the-shelf single-cell sequencing kits. The results will accelerate selection
of therapeutic antibodies and cell therapies, supporting faster development of treatments that improve health,
extend life, and reduce illness.

title: Precision screening in self-collected samples to reduce cervical cancer disparities among Latinas
text:
The goal of this project is to demonstrate the feasibility for the commercialization of the CervicalMethDx
Test, a precision methylation test in self-collected samples to stratify Latina women for high risk of cervical 
cancer. Latinas have the highest cervical cancer prevalence and incidence rates in United States and Puerto 
Rico. A highly sensitive and specific risk test on self-collected samples will enable a novel precision 
medicine paradigm, enabling a reduction in cervical cancer disparities in US and ex-US communities.

title: Zygotic Genome Activation by Maternal Transcription Factors and Epigenetic Modifiers
text:
Understanding how the naive genome of the early embryo is progressively modified to control
gene expression in time and space remains a central challenge in biology. We study the
transition from fertilization to zygotic genome activation, which marks a critical window during
which maternal transcription factors and epigenetic regulators reprogram the parental genomes
to establish totipotency and initiate embryonic development. Leveraging the unique advantages
of the Xenopus system, we aim to resolve a fundamental biological question: how maternal
cues shape the early epigenome and regulatory landscape, from nucleosome-level regulation to
large-scale genome organization.

title: Investigating the Human Virome Using Deep RNA-seq: Supplement to: The Oro-Respiratory-Gut Virome Axis over Space and Time
text:
The human body is inhabited in and on many body sites by a diverse population of viruses (the
virome), and the composition of the virome and how the virome affects human health and disease
is not well understood. Viruses may be comprised of DNA or RNA, but RNA viruses are
particularly difficult to analyze. This supplement will allow very deep analysis of the RNA viruses
within the human virome.

title: Expanding the cancer paralog genetic interaction map to enable precision oncology
text:
Targeted therapies have improved lung cancer patient survival, but not all tumors harbor druggable targets and
those that do invariably develop drug resistance. New drug targets are needed that could be used alone or in
combination with existing therapies to improve patient survival. Here we will develop a new therapeutic approach
based on a concept called “synthetic lethality” and validate this approach as a therapeutic strategy for
suppressing cancer growth and drug resistance.

title: SonoHeal: Smart Resonating Closed-loop Airway Clearance Technology
text:
Airway Clearance Therapy (ACT) is essential for Non-Cystic Fibrosis Bronchiectasis (NCFB) and Cystic
Fibrosis (CF) patients to clear mucus, prevent infections, and reduce exacerbations. Current ACT devices
rely on non-adaptive mechanical vibrations, leading to ineffective, uncomfortable, and lengthy therapy
sessions. SonoHeal is the first closed-loop ACT device that uses real-time airway resistance feedback and
machine learning-driven adaptive therapy to optimize oscillatory pressure waves closer to resonant
frequencies, reducing therapy time, intensity, and improving adherence.

title: CRCNS: Investigating how neural dynamics transition along the time-frequency axis across scales
text: While extensive evidence has shown the importance of whole-person approaches to physical and mental health, existing therapeutic interventions for neurological and mental disorders remain largely single-scale and segregated. The brain, in contrast, is a vastly multiscale and interconnected complex system, and neural dynamics transform dramatically across spatiotemporal scales, internal states, and external contexts. In particular, numerous bodies of neuroscience research have discovered methods for describing brain (dys)function in the time domain, whereas many parallel, largely disconnected efforts have discovered ways to characterize neural dynamics in the frequency domain. The goal of this project is to integrate the complementary dimensions of time and frequency into a unifying theory through the development of causal discovery methods across broad spatiotemporal scales, internal states, and external contexts. Based on extensive preliminary data, our central hypothesis (CH) is that causal mechanisms in complex networked systems such as the brain can be discovered more accurately and robustly in the frequency domain under (both of) two conditions: sufficient spatiotemporal averaging and sufficient stationarity of underlying dynamics. We test our CH through three Specific Aims, each of which combines formal mathematical analysis, causal algorithm design, large-scale numerical simulations, and in vivo electrophysiology and calcium imaging. Aim 1 tests the working hypothesis (WH) that stationary macroscopic causal mechanisms can be learned more robustly and accurately in the frequency domain. Aim 2 then tests the WH that mesoscopic causal mechanisms can best be understood using a novel form of integrated time-frequency analysis that avoids using conventional, Fourier-based decompositions, while Aim 3 tests the WH that macroscopic causal network mechanisms can be more accurately discovered using time-domain methods during the transient period following extrinsic events. The proposed research is thus highly synergistic with the NCCIH Strategic Plan, especially “Objective 1: Advance fundamental science and methods development”. Through the development of innovative causal discovery methods, the proposed research provides the computational theory needed to identify optimal intervention targets across scales and conditions. This project pioneers a transition from conventional, single-scale to a causal, systems understanding of neural information processing. Consequently, it will lay a rigorous foundation for much-needed holistic and multi-scale intervention design for neurological and mental disorders. RELEVANCE (See instructions): This project is relevant to public health because it develops an integrated framework for determining (1) where (at what nodes) and (2) how (in what “language”) to intervene for brain-related disorders. We achieve (1) by developing methods for identifying causal network mechanisms across broad spatiotemporal scales. We achieve (2) by developing a complex-systems theory to determine which analysis domain—time or frequency—is most appropriate for answering which sets of questions, at what scale, and why.

title: Optimizing the HIV Prevention and Care Continua in the United States
text: Getting to zero new infections in the US will require curbing the epidemic among Black and Latino trans women and men who have sex with men – or sexual and gender minorities of color (SGMoC). Intersectionality is an essential but underused framework in population health among SGMoC at elevated risk for HIV. The House and Ball Community (HBC) is a population that faces intersectional stigma and is underserved in the response to HIV. Research and interventions with the HBC have the potential to address intersectionality and transcend geographical boundaries to reach regions most impacted by HIV. Our proposal, One Ballroom, is a national mixed methods longitudinal population-based study of intersectional HIV stigma, and HIV prevention and care among SGMoC in the HBC. This study is the first step in a program of research that will lead to a stigma reduction intervention and includes a 3-year longitudinal qualitative phase, a 12-month longitudinal social epidemiologic phase, and an intensive longitudinal ecological momentary assessment phase.

title: Unraveling the impact of NUP98-HOXA9 on DNA damage responses
text:
Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is an aggressive blood cancer driven by the combined effects of genetic
alterations and DNA damage from environmental and endogenous sources. A recurrent, high-risk consequence
of such exposures is the formation of NUP98 fusion proteins, including NUP98-HOXA9, which are strongly
associated with poor prognosis in both pediatric and adult AML. This project will define how NUP98-HOXA9
affects DNA repair and genome stability, revealing new mechanisms by which environmental exposures promote
AML, identifying new therapeutic targets, and advancing the NIEHS mission to understand and mitigate
environmental impacts on human health.

title: DNA nanodevices for molecular interrogation and regulation of lymphocytes in adaptive immune system
text:
The proposed research will use DNA nanotechnology to develop a new generation of molecular tension probes
and nanodevices to be used in mechanobiology and structural biology. If successful, the project will provide
answers to many important questions related to T cell signaling and activation, and impact the development of
new immunotherapeutic methods. It will also open up a new paradigm for understanding mechano-biological
processes involving other protein mechanosensors.

title: Planarian behavioral screening of ToxCast Phase I chemicals to determine context of use
text:
There is an imminent need to develop high-throughput non-animal models that can replace, refine, and/or reduce
(“3Rs”) animal toxicity testing to better understand the health impacts of the thousands of chemicals that we
encounter in our environment. This is especially true for understanding how chemicals affect the developing
nervous system, which has been undertested due to the extreme cost and time requirement of traditional animal
testing. The goal of this research is to use a large, well characterized library of chemicals to evaluate the utility
and context of use of high-throughput behavioral screening using freshwater planarians as an invertebrate
method for neurotoxicity and developmental neurotoxicity screening.

title: Investigating the landscape and genetic architecture of germline mutagenesis
text:
All genetic diseases, cancers, and evolutionary innovations ultimately begin with genetic mutations. Despite
the fundamental role that mutagenesis plays in human health, we know little about the genetic factors that deter-
mine how many mutations we are likely to transmit to our offspring, and it is unclear whether these same genes
also determine how we accumulate mutations in our bodies as we age. We propose strategies for identifying
genes that cause mutation rates to vary within species and among tissues with the aim of illuminating how the
evolution of lifespan might be functionally linked to the rates of birth defects in future generations.

title: Molecular drivers of tauopathies in stem cell models from diverse human populations
text:
This research and training plan will provide advanced training in stem cell biology and functional genomics that
will support a career in cutting-edge neurodegenerative disease research. These innovative approaches will be
used to develop novel stem cell models from donors of diverse populations and to define the molecular
mechanisms underlying genetic risk for tauopathy.

title: Plasticity and Function of Dopamine Circuits Regulating the Transition to Habit
text:
A range of neuropsychiatric disorders, including obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) and addiction, are
theorized to involve maladaptive habit formation, contributing to compulsions and disruptive repetitive behavior.
Current approaches to treating these disorders are limited because we lack a solid foundation for understanding
the basic neurobiological processes that go awry to produce symptoms. This project focuses on answering
fundamental questions about the neural circuit mechanisms underlying habit formation and motor skill acquisition
with the ultimate goal of deciphering how dysfunction in these circuits contributes to OCD, addiction, and other
neuropsychiatric disorders.

title: Artificial intelligence enabled Stroma-Weighted Automated Grading system to improve risk stratification in Black Men
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because it focuses on the development of an AI-enabled
stroma-weighted automated Gleason grading system (SWAG) for early risk stratification of prostate cancer in
Black men. Once such a strategy is developed there is potential for faster adoption in routine clinical
decisions and risk stratification. Thus, the proposed research is relevant to the NIH's mission and goals that
pertain to enhancing health and reducing illness by early diagnosis of prostate cancer.

title: Targeting Membrane Environments: The Role of Oleate Hydratase (OhyA) in Lipid-Protein Interactions Across Microbial Communities
text:
The research on oleate hydratase (OhyA) promises significant contributions to our understanding of bacterial
physiology and human health applications. By elucidating how OhyA interacts with bacterial membranes to
access and modify fatty acids, this study addresses fundamental questions about protein targeting and
enzymatic function in host lipid-rich environments. This knowledge will enhance our grasp of microbial ecology
and host-microbe interactions within diverse anatomical sites, and also holds the potential for developing novel
biocatalysts and therapeutic strategies aimed at modulating inflammation and metabolic disorders through
targeted lipid interventions.

title: Calcium encoding mechanisms in a model plant
text:
Calcium (Ca) is a ubiquitous second messenger in all eukaryotes ranging
from budding yeast, plants, to human. Defects in Ca signaling cause
numerous human diseases including Alzheimer’s disease, heart failure,
metabolic diseases, immune disorders, neurodegenerative diseases, and
cancer. Proposed research will contribute to the understanding of the basic
conceptual framework of calcium signaling mechanisms highly relevant to
human health.

title: SCH: Counterfactual Explanations for AI-Assisted Cancer Diagnosis and Subtyping
text:
Accurate diagnosis of cancer hinges on histopathological assessment, with treatment
pivoting upon the tumor's morphological classification. AI models can often accurately
classify tumors from histopathological images, but their lack of interpretability severely
hinders their deployment in clinical scenarios. This project develops a principled framework
to systematically explain AI histopathological models using counterfactual explanations,
thereby substantially improving AI-assisted cancer diagnosis for pathologists.

title: Next-Gen Fluorescent Indicators for Imaging Synaptic Zinc in Cortical Sound Processing
text:
Zn2+ is an essential neuromodulator, and dysregulation of synaptic Zn2+ has been linked to numerous
neurological disorders, such as stroke/ischemia, epilepsy, depression, Alzheimer’s disease, and hearing
disorders. This project aims to develop new technology for imaging synaptic Zn2+ secretion in awake behaving
animals and study the roles of Zn2+ in cortical sound processing. This project will pave the way toward
elucidating connections between Zn2+ signaling, information processing, and neurological disorders.

title: Mechanisms of Spindle Position Control by Cortical Cdc42 Waves
text:
Proper spindle positioning is critical for tissue morphogenesis, cell fate specification, and development, and
varies among symmetric and asymmetric divisions, while disruption of spindle positioning has been linked to the
pathology of neurological diseases. While the machinery responsible for anchoring and moving the spindle is
well-characterized, key features of its dynamic regulation are poorly understood, particularly in vertebrates. I
seek to characterize how such features work and how they make flexible control of spindle positioning possible.
